name: Problem Sensitivity
definition: The ability to tell when something is wrong or is likely to go wrong. It does not involve solving the problem, only recognizing that there is a problem.

benchmark.name: MVTec AD
benchmark.metric: image-level AUROC (%), averaged over all 15 MVTec AD classes
benchmark.human_reference: Specialist workforce: industrial visual quality-control inspectors, i.e. people whose job is to spot defective parts and surfaces.

benchmark.name: MVTec AD
benchmark.metric: image-level anomaly detection AUROC (%), mean over 15 MVTec AD categories
benchmark.human_reference: Specialist workforce: industrial visual quality inspectors (median trained inspector), who judge whether a part or texture image shows a defect after seeing examples of normal parts.

benchmark.name: MVTec LOCO AD
benchmark.metric: mean image-level detection AUROC (%), averaged over 5 categories, with logical and structural anomalies weighted equally by the official evaluation script
benchmark.human_reference: Industrial visual quality-control inspectors (specialist workforce) who know the product's specification: what a correct assembly or package should contain and look like.

benchmark.name: BIG-Bench Mistake
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: adults who routinely review and check others' reasoning or work, such as QA reviewers, analysts, and editors, working carefully on short procedural traces.

benchmark.name: ProcessBench
benchmark.metric: F1 (%), the harmonic mean of accuracy on erroneous and correct samples, averaged across the four subsets
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce that checks quantitative reasoning at work, such as math and STEM teachers, graders, tutors, and analysts who review others' step-by-step work. This is not olympiad specialists.

benchmark.name: ProcessBench
benchmark.metric: average F1 (%) across the GSM8K, MATH, OlympiadBench and Omni-MATH subsets; F1 = harmonic mean of accuracy on erroneous and correct samples
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce that checks mathematical reasoning at work, such as math teachers, tutors, graders and STEM-trained analysts. This is not olympiad coaches or research mathematicians.

benchmark.name: ProcessBench
benchmark.metric: Average F1 (%), the harmonic mean of accuracy on erroneous and on correct samples, averaged over the four subsets
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce that reviews quantitative reasoning at work, such as math and STEM teachers, graders, tutors and quantitatively trained analysts. This is not olympiad specialists or the PhD-level expert annotators who made the labels.
